findings.issue: The esbuild onLoad guard rejects inputs outside `root` via relative-path string checks, but esbuild metafile input paths on Windows use backslash-relative forms that `relative()` already normalizes; the check is correct, though '..' prefixes only test one separator form — acceptable given tests run per-platform.
findings.minimalFix: None required; optionally assert `metaInputs` are all under `root` with `startsWith(root + sep)` for clarity.

findings.issue: The test asserts the resolved protection value equals {} but does not assert a positive protection case, so a Worker that always reports empty protection would still pass; this is a pre-existing scope limitation of a test-only integrity delta, not a new defect.
findings.minimalFix: Optionally seed a session snapshot before readProtectionInWorker and assert the closure is returned.

findings.issue: Copying the root package.json wholesale into the emitted tree may pull unrelated script/type metadata, but `packages: 'external'` bundling keeps behavior unchanged; harmless for the test's purpose.
findings.minimalFix: Optionally write a minimal `{"type":"module"}` package.json instead.

limitations: Static review only; actual Worker execution, verifyArtifact implementation, production store graph files (protected-observation-reader, file-session-reader, session-store modules), and CI behavior could not be executed or inspected beyond supplied sources.
The Windows SDK build step producing data/verification/windows artifacts is asserted but not shown; integrity of those binaries is delegated to the previously approved verifyArtifact.
ESM/CJS interplay under NodeNext with extensionless JSON package.json type and emitted .js resolution relies on runtime verification reported as passing; not independently confirmed here.

The mock of node:worker_threads maps only the exact source-file URL to the compiled entry; any unrelated Worker construction in the same module graph would bypass the mock — assumed out of scope for this narrow test-only delta.
